verdicts.why: Finding something unexpectedly is a plain event; the word takes no side on what is found or who finds it.
Seeing or learning something for the first time is described without any attitude toward it.
A technical identifying sense; wholly descriptive.
Playing an accompaniment is a plain musical action with no judgement attached.
Becoming attached names a bond or fondness as its meaning; the speaker's own stance toward it is not built in.
A legal term of art for seizing property as security; it describes the procedure without judging it.
Eating everything on one's plate is stated flatly; no approval or disapproval is carried by the word.
Applying a surface finish is a plain craft action.
Ending a relationship is an unpleasant referent, but the word itself is the plain neighbour, not a loaded alternative.
Timbre is a neutral acoustic property; the word neither praises nor dismisses the sound.
The ordinary members of a body are named without contempt or esteem; 'the ranks' is the plain term.
A neutral collective term for the membership of a group.
A physics label for a quark flavour; no attitude possible.
A declaration of faith is named descriptively; the word does not imply sincerity or its lack.
The right hand is a plain body part.
A turn to the right is pure direction.
A legal or customary entitlement is named neutrally; the word does not express the speaker's approval of the claim.
The political right is a conventional label used by supporters and opponents alike; it identifies rather than judges.
A baseball field position; purely locative.
Regarding something in a certain way is stated neutrally; any judgement lives in the adverb, not the verb.
Handling a subject in speech or art is a plain descriptive verb.
Subjecting something to a process is technical and attitude-free.
Paying for someone's food or drink is a pleasant act, but the pleasantness is the meaning; the word carries no attitude beyond it.
Negotiating toward an agreement is a formal, neutral term.
Guaranteeing payment is a financial action described without judgement.
